content:
Hour and minute hands align at times
\[
t=\frac{12k}{11}\text{ hours},\quad k=0,1,\dots,10.
\]
At these times, their common angle is \(\frac{360k}{11}\) degrees.

The second hand’s angle at time \(t\) hours is
\[
21600t \pmod{360}.
\]
For all three to align:
\[
21600\cdot \frac{12k}{11} \equiv \frac{360k}{11} \pmod{360}.
\]
This simplifies to
\[
\frac{719k}{11}\in\mathbb Z.
\]
Since \(\gcd(719,11)=1\), we need \(11\mid k\). For \(k=0,\dots,10\), only \(k=0\) works.

Thus all three hands align only at 12:00 in each 12-hour period, so twice per day.

\[
\boxed{2}
\]
